title: The receptive helper verb (passive)
summary: れる / られる means "to receive or get" the action of the verb before it. The receiver is the main carriage, and the real doer is marked with に.

blocks.text: Textbooks call this the "passive" and label it a conjugation. The course prefers **receptive helper verb**, because that is what it does: it makes a verb that means "to get" or "to receive" the action. Both names point at the same form. What matters is that the particles keep doing their usual jobs.
Attach the helper to the **あ-stem** (the same stem ない uses). Godan: **れる**. Ichidan: **られる**. It looks exactly like the ichidan potential られる, but real sentences make the difference clear.
The engine of the sentence is **れる / られる**, so the main carriage is the one who **receives**. It does not have to be a person.

Keep the receptive in **two separate verbs**: the attached verb (叱る) is done by someone else, and the head verb れる is done by the receiver, who "gets" it. In 叱られた someone else scolds and Sakura does the getting. So, unlike the potential (読める), the two verbs must never be merged into one.
Compare two directions. When you **push** something toward a target, に marks the target. れる is a **pull** verb, so に marks the **source** the thing is pulled from, not a target.

blocks.jp: （私が）さくらにボールを投げた。
blocks.en: (I) threw the ball to Sakura. (push: に = target)

blocks.text: 水が犬に飲まれた。 に marks the source of the pull.

blocks.en: The water got drunk by the dog.

blocks.jp: かばんが誰かに盗まれた。
blocks.en: The bag was stolen by someone.

blocks.text: Japanese also uses the receptive when something happens **to a person** and it bothers them. Textbooks call it the "nuisance receptive" (迷惑受け身). The affected person becomes the main carriage (が), while the thing that was taken keeps its **を**. Compare the two versions.
さくらが誰かにかばんを盗まれた。 Sakura is the receiver.

blocks.title: Bag stolen, two ways
rows: さくらは誰かにかばんが盗まれた。
さくらが誰かにかばんを盗まれた。

blocks.jp: さくらが誰かにかばんを盗まれた。
blocks.en: Sakura had her bag stolen by someone.

blocks.title: Remember
items: **あ-stem + れる** (godan), **られる** (ichidan): "to get X-ed".
The **receiver** is the main carriage (**が**). The **doer** takes **に**.
The suffering receptive: **person が + other に + thing を + 〜られた**.
Do not mix it up with the potential: **食べられる** can be either, and the sentence tells you which.

questions.note: あ-stem 読ま + れる.
Ichidan verbs take られる.

questions.prompt: 生徒が先生＿＿ほめられた。
questions.note: The doer of a receptive sentence takes に.
questions.en: The student was praised by the teacher.

questions.note: 弟 is the receiver and 姉に marks the doer, so the engine is receptive.
questions.en: The little brother was woken up early by his older sister.

questions.note: に marks the doer in a receptive sentence.
questions.en: The child was called by the mother.

questions.note: The one who receives the action takes が.
questions.en: The cake was eaten by my little sister.

questions.prompt: I was laughed at by my friend.
questions.note: 私は is the topic; the hidden が carriage is me, the receiver. 友達に marks the doer.
questions.en: I was laughed at by my friend.

questions.prompt: I had my diary read by my mother.
questions.note: Suffering receptive: the read thing keeps を.
questions.en: I had my diary read by my mother.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "I was praised by the teacher"?
options: 私は先生にほめられた
私が先生にほめさせた
questions.note: 私は is the topic; the hidden が carriage is me, the receiver. 先生に marks the doer.

options: The letter got read by Mom
questions.note: Receiver 手紙が, doer 母に: the receptive.
questions.en: The letter was read by Mom.

questions.note: The doer takes に; the bitten leg keeps を.
questions.en: I was bitten on the leg by a dog.

questions.prompt: 兄が母に叱られた。 The one who scolded is 母.
questions.note: に marks the doer.
questions.en: My older brother was scolded by Mother.

questions.instruction: Which is the あ-stem of 書く?
questions.note: The receptive attaches to the same stem as ない.

questions.instruction: Which is the receptive of 言う?
questions.note: う becomes わ before れる.

options: 本が先生に読まれている
questions.note: The doer must take に, not を.

questions.instruction: Who is bothered by what happened?
questions.prompt: 私は弟にケーキを食べられた。
questions.note: The suffering receptive: the affected person is the main carriage.
questions.en: My little brother ate my cake (and it bothered me).

questions.prompt: In a receptive sentence the doer is marked with を.
questions.note: The doer takes に: れる is a pull verb.

questions.instruction: Which sentence makes the window the main carriage?
questions.note: Receiver が, doer に, られる.

questions.instruction: Tap the thing taken from the receiver (the を word)
questions.note: In the suffering receptive the affected thing keeps を.
questions.en: My older brother ate my cake.

questions.prompt: The photo was seen by my friend.
questions.note: Receiver が, doer に, receptive verb.
questions.en: The photo was seen by my friend.

questions.instruction: What do れる / られる do to a verb?
options: Someone is made to do it
questions.note: れる / られる is the receptive helper verb.
あ-stem 呼ば + れる.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says my brother himself was bothered?
options: 弟は誰かに自転車が盗まれた。
弟が誰かに自転車を盗まれた。
弟が誰かに自転車を盗んだ。
弟を誰かに自転車が盗まれた。
questions.note: The bothered person is the main carriage, and the stolen thing keeps を.
questions.en: My younger brother had his bicycle stolen by someone.
